title: NZ School Holiday Dates 2025–2027 — Planning Guide
meta_desc: Official NZ school holiday dates for 2025, 2026 and 2027: all four breaks, term dates, Easter and the public holidays that affect family travel.
intro: New Zealand has four school holiday breaks a year, and the Ministry of Education sets the term dates nationally, so every state school gets the same four breaks. Only small things differ between schools: when Term 1 starts, when Term 4 ends, teacher-only days, and private or integrated schools. This guide gives the official dates for 2025–2027, the Easter dates that move around them, and the public holidays that change what's open and what it costs.
key_takeaway: NZ school holidays are national: the same April, July, late September–October and December–January breaks for every state school. 2026: 3–19 Apr, 4–19 Jul, 26 Sep–11 Oct, then summer from 19 Dec. 2027: 10–26 Apr, 3–18 Jul, 25 Sep–10 Oct, then summer from 18 Dec. Only the Term 1 start and Term 4 end vary a little by school. Easter moves: 5 Apr 2026, 28 Mar 2027. July = ski season peak; summer needs bookings 2–3 months ahead.

sections.heading: Easter Dates (Moving Holiday) 2025–2027
sections.body: Easter dates move every year. In 2025 and 2026 Easter falls inside the April school holidays. In 2027 Easter is early (28 March), so it falls in Term 1 and the long weekend comes about two weeks before the autumn break starts on 10 April.

sections.heading: Teacher-Only Days (Non-Student Days)
sections.body: Teacher-only days are days when teachers work but students stay home. Each school sets its own, usually around the start or end of a term, so the dates differ by school, not by region. Your school's calendar will list them. They are separate from the four national holiday breaks.

sections.heading: Plan Each 2026 Holiday — Activity Guides & Booking Windows
sections.body:
Each NZ school holiday has its own character, weather, and booking rhythm. Here's how to plan each one, with links to our detailed activity guides for every period.

Winter (July) — peak ski season. July is the busiest, most expensive holiday for snow travel. Queenstown, Wanaka, and Ruapehu fill first; book accommodation 3–4 months ahead (April for July travel) and buy ski lift passes before you arrive. The Skyline luge in Queenstown can hit 45-minute waits mid-morning — go at 9am opening or after 3pm. Wellington's Zealandia night tours (only three per night) sell out 6+ weeks ahead. See our full NZ winter school holidays activities guide, plus city-specific picks for Auckland, Wellington, and Christchurch winter 2026.

Summer (December–January) — the big one. Six weeks long and overlapping Christmas and New Year. Coastal destinations book out 8–12 weeks ahead; the Coromandel and Bay of Islands fill 3+ months in advance. Campervans sell out by September and Top 10 holiday parks by August. Expect premium pricing — accommodation can be 2–3× normal cost over Boxing Day to early January. Start planning now with our summer school holidays 2026/27 guide.

Autumn (April) — best value, settled weather. Mild 15–20°C days, golden light, and far fewer crowds. Hawke's Bay, Rotorua, and the wine regions shine. Accommodation books 4–6 weeks ahead rather than months. Easter falls inside this break in 2026 — see our NZ Easter holiday ideas and Easter 2027 guide.

Spring (September–October) — the underrated one. Warming up (12–18°C), thinning crowds, and lower prices. Abel Tasman, Nelson, and the top of the South Island are ideal. Book 4–6 weeks ahead for the best value-to-experience ratio of the year.

For a calendar view of every holiday with destination suggestions, see the NZ school holidays hub.

sections.heading: Why Dates Can Differ Between Schools
sections.body:
New Zealand's term and holiday dates are national: the Ministry of Education sets them for all state schools, so there are no regional holiday zones. What can differ:

- **Term 1 start:** a window rather than one date — 26 Jan to 9 Feb in 2026, and 28 Jan to 3 Feb in 2027, depending on the school
- **Term 4 end:** 'no later than' Fri 18 Dec 2026 and Fri 17 Dec 2027; some schools finish a few days earlier
- **Teacher-only days:** set by each school
- **Private, integrated and kura schools:** may set their own dates, so check with yours

Always confirm with your child's school before you book non-refundable travel.

faq.question: Do all NZ schools have the same holiday dates?
faq.answer: Yes, for state schools. The Ministry of Education sets the term and holiday dates nationally, so the four breaks (April, July, late September–October, December–January) are the same everywhere. Only the Term 1 start and Term 4 end can vary a little by school, and private or integrated schools may differ. Check your child's school before booking.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit NZ with school-age kids?
faq.answer: Autumn (April school holidays) or spring (October school holidays) offer the best balance — fewer crowds, good weather, and moderate pricing. July has great skiing but is busiest and most expensive. Summer (Dec–Jan) is beach season but extremely crowded and expensive. If visiting from overseas, autumn and spring are most family-friendly.

faq.question: When is Easter in 2026 and 2027?
faq.answer: Easter 2026: Sunday 5 April (Good Friday 3 April, Easter Monday 6 April), which falls inside the autumn school holidays. Easter 2027: Sunday 28 March (Good Friday 26 March, Easter Monday 29 March), which falls in Term 1, about two weeks before the autumn break starts on 10 April.

faq.question: How far ahead should I book activities during school holidays?
faq.answer: For July (ski season) and Dec–Jan (summer): book 2–3 months ahead and popular experiences 6–8 weeks ahead. For April and October: book 4–6 weeks ahead. Zealandia night tours (Wellington) need 6+ weeks' notice. Ski lift passes should be booked before you arrive in July.

faq.question: Are teacher-only days the same as school holidays?
faq.answer: No — teacher-only days are when teachers work but students don't attend (5–8 per year). School holidays are when the whole school closes. Teachers use these days for professional development and planning. Each school sets its own teacher-only days, so check your school's calendar.

faq.question: Can I find the exact dates for my child's school?
faq.answer: Yes — check your school's website directly, or contact them by email. You can also check the Ministry of Education website (https://www.education.govt.nz) for the national term dates. Individual schools sometimes add extra teacher-only days or term breaks.
